thread:
maria: quick heads-up — during the last deprec rollout we saw many clients flip between v2 and v1 on short timescales which inflated error noise and made telemetry churn. thinking about a "sticky grace" routing idea to stabilize fallbacks.

evan: sticky grace? like pinning a token to the last-served version for a short TTL so it doesn't oscillate?

maria: exactly. when a request falls back from v2 to v1 due to compatibility, routing adds a server-side affinity for that token: `route_affinity=v1` with a TTL (eg 2m). subsequent requests in TTL prefer the served version.

dan: that would reduce repeated fallthrough churn. question: attribution - do we count those as v1 immediately or keep original inbound attribution?

maria: plan is to attribute consumption to the actually served variant for billing/telemetry. but we also emit `affinity.origin=fallthrough` so console can show it was a fallback-affinity.

tasha: console UX request: show a small badge on route usage: "fallback-affinity active" with count + TTL histogram. customers should understand why route distribution looks weird.

lucy: curious about quotas — if affinity pins to v1 but original request was going to v2, do we shift quota consumption to v1? that affects billing and quota enforcement.

maria: yes shift to served variant for quota calculation. to avoid abuse, affinity only created when cohort is whitelisted (canaries, internal experiments) or when tenant-level opt-in for migration smoothing is enabled. default behavior remains conservative.

evan: security/abuse vector: client could spoof affinity. must be server-side only; edge inserts affinity entries in routing store. ignore any client-provided `x-route-affinity`.

dan: implementation notes: routing will write an affinity entry keyed by token_id -> { served_variant, reason=fallthrough, ttl }. affinity lookups run before route selection. must be fast (cache + async eviction).

lucy: caching concern: affinity can increase uneven load on older variants. we should add a circuit to avoid overwhelming v1 pools: if affinity count for v1 > threshold, we degrade affinity acceptance. maybe a dynamic cap per-variant.

maria: agreed. add a soft cap: if affinity_rate(v1) > 0.05 of sustained traffic for 5m, stop creating new affinities to v1 and emit `affinity.rejected_capacity`.

tasha: telemetry: emit events `affinity.created`, `affinity.expired`, `affinity.rejected_capacity`, with tags: tenant, cohort, origin_route, served_variant. console will show time series for `affinity.created_rate`.

evan: quota smoothing for tenants doing mass migration: add a temporary smoothing window where sudden spikes from migration don't trigger hard enforcement. i.e., quota-service can apply a smoothing factor for N hours on a per-tenant migration flag.

maria: risk: we can't let customers bypass quotas. smoothing means raising alerting thresholds and applying graduated throttles, not removing enforcement. say: allow soft-burst up to +20% for 1h, then step down.

dan: operational runbook: enable tenant opt-in via console: "Migration smoothing (opt-in)" with fields {window_hours, soft_burst_pct}. default OFF. enable only for tenants with verified contact.

lucy: billing: need clear audit tags so finance can separate migration smoothing from normal billing. include `migration_smoothing=true` on telemetry and export rows.

maria: good call. also add `affinity.audit_id` when we create affinity for a tenant so exports link records.

tasha: UX copy: "Migration smoothing and fallback affinity — opt-in tools to reduce noisy fallbacks and steady route behavior during version transitions. Affinity pins served variant briefly; smoothing allows controlled bursts. Beta; contact support to opt-in."

evan: dev tasks: routing: affinity store + insertion logic + capacity rejection metric. quota-service: accept smoothing flags and apply soft burst rules. console: per-tenant toggle + affinity UI. telemetry: events + export hooks.

dan: edge cases: long-running streaming sessions — affinity should not override established streaming session route. affinity only applies to new requests.

lucy: also add TTL variant: default 120s for simple fallthroughs, longer (up to 24h) for explicit migration opt-ins where tenant requests long lived pin. make longer only via console.

maria: security: affinity state must be space-scoped and tenant-authorized. only edge/routing service can write. sign affinity writes in trace.

tasha: monitoring: dashboards for `affinity.created_rate`, `affinity.expiry_rate`, `affinity.rejected_capacity`, `smoothing.overquota_incidents`. alert if affinity.rejected_capacity > 1% sustained.

evan: timeline: prototype in routing canary in 1 week, telemetry + console follow in parallel. small internal tenant test, then invite-only customer beta.

dan: I'll sketch a short RFC and PR for routing affinity store. linking when ready.

maria: thanks. if everyone OK ill add to roadmap and start RFC.

ops-bot: routing/affinity feature flagged deploy scheduled to canary at 2024-12-02T18:00:00Z.

maria: awesome. we'll validate metrics for 72h and reconvene.
